title: kdash panel control
description: Payload of kdash:panel:{host} - latest-value, ts-owned, no TTL. Tells the dashboard running on {host} which screen it should be showing. The key is exactly 3 segments and {host} is authoritative; the payload carries no echo of it. The consumer acts on a CHANGE of ts, never on the current value: a republish with an unchanged ts is the same command, and a command older than the reader's window (60 s in libkdash) is never replayed at all. That is what keeps a remote command from fighting a human at the keyboard, and what lets the read side stay read-only - no GETDEL, no consumed-means-handled.

want.description: Which screen the panel should show. The enum is closed: an unrecognised word rejects the record rather than being guessed at.

ts.description: Unix seconds (float): the COMMAND's time, not the writer's heartbeat. Advancing it is what issues a new command, so it is required and positive - a stamp a consumer cannot compare is no command at all.
